name: Alley cropping
definition: Planted woody rows with annual crops cultivated in the alleys between them; distinguish this row-and-alley arrangement from dispersed trees and boundary-only planting.
dominant_limiting_factor: Cultivable host land and biophysical conditions for trees and annual crops.
grouping_rationale: Shares the cultivable-land envelope with dispersed trees in annual crops. Soft management access is assessed through operational risk; hard legal exclusions remain structural masks.
references: ["Nair 1993", "Zomer et al. 2014", "https://www.fao.org/agroforestry/about-agroforestry/faqs/ (examples of agroforestry systems)", "Method decision agroforestry_family_definitions; configuration/agroforestry-definitions.md"]

name: Dispersed trees with annual crops
definition: Planted trees dispersed within annual-crop fields. This catalogue distinguishes dispersed arrangements from deliberate crop alleys and boundary-only woody lines; broader source terminology is retained in evidence.
dominant_limiting_factor: Cultivable host land and biophysical conditions for trees and annual crops.
grouping_rationale: Shares the planted-silvoarable host envelope with alley cropping. This display clarification does not retrospectively reclassify broadly worded source claims.

name: Planted boundary / live fence on cropland
definition: Planted woody lines on cultivated-field boundaries for demarcation, live fencing or another documented purpose. Boundary location alone does not establish wind protection or runoff control.
dominant_limiting_factor: Observed cultivated-field boundary geometry and compatible host/establishment conditions.
grouping_rationale: Boundary location defines this placement family. Wind and contour functions require their own evidence and placement logic. A candidate zone is not planted pixel area; estimate physical footprint separately from supported geometry and width.

name: Farmer-managed natural regeneration (FMNR)
definition: Farmer protection and management of naturally occurring woody regrowth from living stumps, roots or seed on farmland. Overlaps with assisted natural regeneration; the management label alone does not require a separate suitability surface.
dominant_limiting_factor: Viable natural regrowth or recruitment potential on farmland.
grouping_rationale: Shares natural-regeneration context with assisted regeneration. Tenure security is an operational-risk condition, not a structural exclusion. State whether each mapping addresses recruitment or retention of existing trees.

name: Parkland tree retention
definition: Retention and management of existing scattered trees on farmland; natural regeneration can renew the stand. Retaining existing trees does not itself demonstrate current recruitment potential.
dominant_limiting_factor: Existing farm-tree assets for retention; viable regrowth or seed sources where recruitment is proposed.
grouping_rationale: Retained with farmland regeneration for catalogue continuity. An accepted mapping must distinguish retention from recruitment; do not impose recruitment requirements on all existing trees. Soft tenure conditions belong in operational risk.

name: Assisted natural regeneration on farmland
definition: Active assistance such as protection, weeding or thinning to support natural woody regeneration on farmland. Related to and overlapping farmer-managed natural regeneration, rather than an exclusive system type.
dominant_limiting_factor: Viable natural regrowth or recruitment potential on farmland.
grouping_rationale: Shares regeneration context with FMNR. Retain source terminology and management differences without inventing independent evidence or separate suitability maps; soft tenure conditions belong in operational risk.

name: Planted trees in grazed pasture
definition: Planted trees or shrubs intentionally managed with forage and grazing livestock on the same land unit. Use agrosilvopasture where a separate cropping component beyond forage is documented; fruit harvested from the trees alone does not establish that component.
dominant_limiting_factor: Compatible tree and forage conditions plus an observed managed grazing system.
grouping_rationale: Retains the livestock family with agrosilvopasture. Establishment and system composition are distinct. This planted ID does not silently include unmanaged woodland grazing or introduce an existing-tree silvopasture pathway.

name: Trees with crops and livestock
definition: Trees or shrubs deliberately integrated with crops and livestock on the same management unit, together or through a documented seasonal rotation. Record the separate cropping component and timing; crops elsewhere on the farm do not establish this classification.
dominant_limiting_factor: Compatible tree, crop and forage conditions plus observed crop-livestock management and timing.
grouping_rationale: Retains the silvopastoral family. A historical grassland-only host gate is insufficient for all mixed crop-livestock systems; new mappings require explicit observed host scope and accepted scientific proposals.

name: Windbreaks & shelterbelts
definition: Woody rows deliberately positioned to reduce damaging wind exposure. They may stand within a field or at its boundary; record location separately from function.
dominant_limiting_factor: Wind exposure and orientation/placement of protective woody rows within a compatible host system.
grouping_rationale: Wind-protection placement differs from generic boundary location and contour/runoff placement. Report candidate zones and geometry-supported physical footprint separately from the area receiving protection. A boundary windbreak is one physical feature.
references: ["Brandle et al. 2004", "https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/sites/default/files/2022-10/Windbreak-Shelterbelt_Establishment_380_NHCP_CPS_2021.pdf (definition and placement criteria)", "Method decision agroforestry_family_definitions; configuration/agroforestry-definitions.md"]

name: Woody contour buffers
definition: Woody strips or rows positioned with respect to contours and runoff pathways to reduce erosion or intercept runoff. Field-boundary placement is optional; non-woody grass strips are not automatically agroforestry.
dominant_limiting_factor: Terrain, contour and runoff-path placement within a compatible host system.
grouping_rationale: Terrain/runoff placement differs from wind exposure and generic boundary placement. Use candidate zones, not planted pixel area. Any quantitative design or suitability rule requires its own source-backed accepted proposal.

name: Shaded perennial-crop system
definition: Shade trees grown over an existing perennial cash crop. The understorey crop (coffee, cocoa, tea, cardamom, pepper, ...) is a PARAMETER of the family, scoped per AOI - not a separate subpractice.
dominant_limiting_factor: The host crop's observed distribution / production (where the crop is actually grown), plus shade-as-adaptation at the climate-stressed edge.
grouping_rationale: One family, crop as a parameter (run per candidate crop, combine by max retaining the driving crop) - the way F1 is not split by tree species. Gated by the crop's observed distribution (MapSPAM / GAEZ / EO commodity maps / ag-stats), not a modelled niche; bioclimatic-envelope modelling is the fallback only where distribution data are absent. Crops are not blended into one envelope (coffee highlands and cocoa lowlands are nearly disjoint).

name: Multistrata homegardens
definition: Intensive multistrata tree-crop gardens adjacent to dwellings, sometimes including livestock. Their homestead context is retained rather than automatically assigning a landscape livestock suitability surface.
dominant_limiting_factor: Settlement and water proximity at sub-pixel scale.
grouping_rationale: Sub-pixel and proximity-driven; retain qualitative implementation guidance without claiming pixel-area footprint or eligibility for new area-based synthesis.
references: ["Kumar & Nair 2004", "https://www.fao.org/agroforestry/about-agroforestry/faqs/ (examples of agroforestry systems)", "Method decision agroforestry_family_definitions; configuration/agroforestry-definitions.md"]

name: Macro-catchment water harvesting
definition: Structures that collect runoff from a catchment larger than the cultivated/storage area (e.g. check dams, farm ponds).
dominant_limiting_factor: Runoff generation + storable terrain (slope, drainage, soil permeability).
grouping_rationale: Runoff-catchment WH practices share a runoff-generation + storage-terrain limiting factor; reported as an applicability zone, not pixel area.

name: Cross-family evidence context
definition: Evidence-scope metadata for explicitly shared agroforestry claims, not a real subpractice. Missing family attribution does not demonstrate applicability to every family.
dominant_limiting_factor: (cross-cutting — applies to all families)
grouping_rationale: Retain this compatibility tag for shared evidence without forcing it into a specific family. Exclude it from intervention choices/counts; inspect actual family applicability before synthesis.

name: Passive natural regeneration
definition: Forest recovery by spontaneous regeneration after the degrading pressure is removed; no planting or active management.
dominant_limiting_factor: regeneration potential: seed-source/remnant proximity, residual woody cover, low disturbance, pressure-removal feasibility
grouping_rationale: Restoration continuum passive end; limited by natural regeneration potential not planting. Grounded stocktake 'natural regeneration' rows + distance-from-remnants variable.

name: Secondary succession
definition: Unassisted secondary forest succession on abandoned/degraded land.
dominant_limiting_factor: same as passive regeneration — spontaneous recovery gated by regeneration potential
grouping_rationale: Grouped with passive regeneration: identical limiting factor (natural propagule supply + low disturbance).

name: Assisted natural regeneration (ANR)
definition: Accelerate natural regeneration by removing barriers (weeding, fire/grazing protection, liberation thinning, releasing wildlings); relies on natural propagules, not planting.
dominant_limiting_factor: partial regeneration potential + intervention feasibility (access/labour/management)
grouping_rationale: Distinct from passive (needs active intervention + access) and from planting (no planting). Middle of the restoration continuum.

name: Reforestation
definition: Deliberate tree planting to re-establish forest on formerly forested land.
dominant_limiting_factor: planting envelope for target species/community + degradation too high for natural regen
grouping_rationale: Active-planting family; reforestation vs afforestation is a prior-land-cover flag, not a separate family (same planting limiting factor).

name: Afforestation
definition: Tree planting to establish forest on land not recently forested.
dominant_limiting_factor: planting envelope for target species + site not previously forest (do-no-harm caveat on non-forest ecosystems)
grouping_rationale: Grouped with reforestation/enrichment under active planting; prior land cover is a context flag.

name: Enrichment planting
definition: Planting target species into degraded/secondary forest to restore composition/structure.
dominant_limiting_factor: planting envelope + existing degraded canopy (partial cover)
grouping_rationale: Active-planting intervention within existing degraded forest; shares the planting limiting factor.

name: Mangrove restoration
definition: Restoration of mangrove/coastal forested wetlands by planting or hydrology restoration.
dominant_limiting_factor: coastal hydrology: tidal hydroperiod, salinity, intertidal elevation, sediment supply, wave energy
grouping_rationale: Distinct coastal-hydrology limiting factor. PARKED from discovery pending scope decision (coastal vs rural-terrestrial scan). | Promoted to its own NbS 2026-10-19 (Pete: mangroves are a separate category of restoration and the World Bank team wants them for a pilot). One family: planting and ecological mangrove restoration share the dominant limiting factors (tidal position / hydroperiod, salinity, coastal geomorphology), which differ in kind from terrestrial forest. Scheme draft in methodology/families/mangrove.md, pending MFL sign-off.

name: Ecological mangrove restoration (EMR)
definition: Restore tidal hydrology and let mangroves regenerate naturally rather than mass-planting.
dominant_limiting_factor: coastal hydrology restoration feasibility (hydroperiod/elevation) + natural propagule supply
grouping_rationale: Grouped with mangrove restoration (same coastal-hydrology driver). PARKED from discovery pending scope decision. | Promoted to its own NbS 2026-10-19 (Pete: mangroves are a separate category of restoration and the World Bank team wants them for a pilot). One family: planting and ecological mangrove restoration share the dominant limiting factors (tidal position / hydroperiod, salinity, coastal geomorphology), which differ in kind from terrestrial forest. Scheme draft in methodology/families/mangrove.md, pending MFL sign-off.

name: Forest protection / avoided degradation
definition: Protecting existing forest under threat from degradation/deforestation.
dominant_limiting_factor: existing standing forest x degradation/deforestation pressure x governance feasibility (governance is soft -> M2b, not T4)
grouping_rationale: Not new establishment; applies within existing-forest mask. PARKED from discovery pending scope decision (restoration family vs separate avoided-deforestation stream).

name: Community-based forest management
definition: Community/collective management of forest for protection and sustainable use.
dominant_limiting_factor: existing forest + community tenure/governance feasibility (soft enabling-env -> M2b)
grouping_rationale: Grouped with protection: same standing-stock+governance driver. PARKED from discovery pending scope decision.

name: Contour bunds / ridges
definition: Earthen bunds or ridges on the contour that hold rain where it falls on the field.
dominant_limiting_factor: On-field water balance: rainfall deficit + soil infiltration/depth, gentle slope; placed on inter-stream slopes.
grouping_rationale: In-situ moisture conservation: capture rain in place, no external catchment or storage; grouped by the on-field water-balance limiter.

name: Planting pits / Zai
definition: Micro-pits that concentrate water and organic matter at the planting station (Zai, tassa).
dominant_limiting_factor: On-field water balance in degraded/crusted soils; rainfall deficit.
grouping_rationale: In-situ point moisture concentration; same on-field water-balance limiter as contour bunds.

name: Conservation tillage / mulching
definition: Residue cover and reduced tillage to cut evaporation and raise infiltration.
dominant_limiting_factor: Soil infiltration/water-holding + rainfall deficit; low slope.
grouping_rationale: In-situ moisture conservation via surface management; on-field water-balance limiter.

name: Semi-circular bunds
definition: Crescent bunds catching runoff from a short bare micro-catchment upslope.
dominant_limiting_factor: Short-slope runoff:cropped-area ratio + slope/soil.
grouping_rationale: Micro-catchment: a small bare catchment feeds an adjacent basin; grouped by the short-slope runoff-ratio limiter.

name: Eyebrow terraces
definition: Small individual terraces harvesting runoff from an upslope strip.
dominant_limiting_factor: Short-slope runoff:planted-area ratio.
grouping_rationale: Micro-catchment runoff-ratio limiter (distinct from slope-reshaping bench terraces).

name: Runoff strips
definition: Alternating bare runoff-donor strips and cropped receiving strips.
dominant_limiting_factor: Runoff-donor:receiver strip ratio + slope/soil.
grouping_rationale: Micro-catchment runoff-ratio limiter.

name: Farm ponds
definition: Excavated/embanked ponds storing runoff from a larger catchment.
dominant_limiting_factor: Runoff generation + drainage geomorphology (3rd-4th order) + soil clay for storage.
grouping_rationale: Ex-situ storage sited within candidate drainage zones; runoff+geomorphology limiter.

name: Check dams
definition: Small barriers across channels to slow flow, trap sediment and recharge.
dominant_limiting_factor: Drainage-line geomorphology (2nd-3rd order stream) + runoff.
grouping_rationale: Ex-situ channel structure; sited on drainage lines, reported as siting density not pixel area.

name: Percolation tanks
definition: Impoundments designed to recharge groundwater by infiltration.
dominant_limiting_factor: Runoff + permeable substrate/lineaments for recharge.
grouping_rationale: Ex-situ recharge structure; runoff+recharge-terrain limiter.

name: Bench terraces
definition: Level or near-level steps cut into a slope to hold water and soil.
dominant_limiting_factor: Slope (defining, ~5-25%) + soil depth for construction.
grouping_rationale: Terracing/slope SWC: slope is the defining variable; distinct slope envelope from in-situ/ex-situ.

name: Stone bunds / fanya juu
definition: Contour stone bunds or fanya juu embankments that progressively terrace a slope.
dominant_limiting_factor: Slope + stone availability + soil depth.
grouping_rationale: Slope-reshaping SWC; grouped with bench terraces by the slope-driven limiter.

name: Rooftop / domestic harvesting
definition: Cisterns/reservoirs capturing roof runoff at buildings.
dominant_limiting_factor: Settlement/building presence (sub-pixel).
grouping_rationale: PARKED: settlement-driven, not a rural-landscape suitability surface (scope Q).

name: Spate / floodwater harvesting
definition: Diversion and spreading of ephemeral flood flows (spate irrigation, jessour, water spreading).
dominant_limiting_factor: Ephemeral channel / wadi presence + sediment load.
grouping_rationale: PARKED: ephemeral-channel gated; thin in stocktake; own family vs fold into ex-situ is a scope Q.

name: Planted grass/herbaceous filter strip
definition: Established herbaceous strip along a watercourse to intercept sediment and nutrients from adjacent runoff.
dominant_limiting_factor: watercourse proximity + riparian slope/width + adjacent-cropland runoff load + planting
grouping_rationale: Planted along-stream placement gated by watercourse proximity + adjacent-land load; grass vs woody is a parameter.
references: ["reference/stocktake/peer_reviewed_benchmarked.csv", "Mayer et al. 2007 (riparian buffer N removal)", "InVEST nutrient retention"]

name: Planted woody/forested riparian buffer
definition: Established trees/shrubs along a watercourse for bank stability, shade and habitat.
dominant_limiting_factor: watercourse proximity + riparian slope/width + planting envelope
grouping_rationale: Same along-stream planted placement limiter as grass strips (vegetation type = parameter).
references: ["reference/stocktake/peer_reviewed_benchmarked.csv", "Mayer et al. 2007 (riparian buffer N removal)", "InVEST nutrient retention"]

name: Riparian natural regeneration
definition: Protect/allow natural regeneration of existing riparian vegetation.
dominant_limiting_factor: watercourse proximity + existing riparian condition / regeneration potential + hydro-connectivity
grouping_rationale: Restoration-based (not planted): gated by existing riparian condition/regen potential.
references: ["reference/stocktake/peer_reviewed_benchmarked.csv", "Mayer et al. 2007 (riparian buffer N removal)", "InVEST nutrient retention"]

name: Riparian reforestation
definition: Restore degraded riparian banks by re-establishing woody vegetation.
dominant_limiting_factor: watercourse proximity + degradation/regen potential of the riparian zone
grouping_rationale: Grouped with natural regeneration: restoration limiter, distinct from planted-buffer establishment.
references: ["reference/stocktake/peer_reviewed_benchmarked.csv", "Mayer et al. 2007 (riparian buffer N removal)", "InVEST nutrient retention"]

name: Wetland restoration / rewetting
definition: Restore a degraded/drained wetland by restoring hydrology (block drainage, re-flood).
dominant_limiting_factor: former/degraded wetland extent + hydrology (water table, drainage history, connectivity)
grouping_rationale: Restore-what-was: gated by degraded wetland extent + hydrology; distinct from creating new wetlands.

name: Drainage blocking / re-flooding
definition: Block artificial drainage to raise the water table and re-flood a former wetland.
dominant_limiting_factor: drainage state + water table + former wetland extent
grouping_rationale: Rewetting mechanism within restoration; same degraded-extent + hydrology limiter.

name: Floodplain wetland reconnection
definition: Reconnect a floodplain wetland body to its water source.
dominant_limiting_factor: hydro-connectivity + former floodplain-wetland extent
grouping_rationale: Restoration by reconnection; targets the wetland body (cf. riparian streamside strip).

name: Wetland creation
definition: Create a new wetland where none currently exists (water storage, habitat, nutrient interception).
dominant_limiting_factor: water availability + low-lying/depression terrain + soil permeability + currently-not-wetland
grouping_rationale: Siting a NEW wetland on non-wetland land: terrain/water-availability limiter, distinct from restore.

name: Wetland reconstruction
definition: Reconstruct/engineer a wetland form on non-wetland land.
dominant_limiting_factor: terrain + water availability + soil
grouping_rationale: Grouped with creation: new-wetland siting limiter.

name: Peatland rewetting
definition: Rewet drained peatland to halt subsidence and restore peat function.
dominant_limiting_factor: peat soil presence + drainage state + water table
grouping_rationale: Peat-specific: peat soil layer + subsidence + carbon make it a distinct variable set.

name: Paludiculture
definition: Productive use of wet/rewetted peat (wet meadow/pasture, reed).
dominant_limiting_factor: peat soil + high water table + suitable wet crop
grouping_rationale: Wet farming of peat; grouped with peatland rewetting by the peat-soil + water-table limiter.

name: Constructed / treatment wetland
definition: Engineered wetland for point-source / agricultural-drainage treatment (e.g. HSSF-CW).
dominant_limiting_factor: point-source / ag-drainage load + engineered siting (area, slope, inflow)
grouping_rationale: PARKED: treatment/engineering siting problem (peri-urban/point-source), scope Q for a rural landscape scan.

name: Tidal marsh / coastal wetland restoration
definition: Restore coastal tidal marsh / salt marsh.
dominant_limiting_factor: coastal hydrology: tidal inundation, salinity, elevation
grouping_rationale: PARKED: coastal-hydrology driver; same coastal scope Q as forest-restoration mangroves.

name: Cross-cutting envelope (family-agnostic)
definition: Tagging value for evidence applying across ALL water-harvesting / SWC families (e.g. pooled "soil and water conservation" results in syntheses and programme evaluations that do not isolate one practice), not one subpractice. Not a real subpractice.
dominant_limiting_factor: (cross-cutting — applies to all families)
grouping_rationale: Meta-tag mirroring agroforestry cross_cutting_envelope (2026-10-05, T3/T6 WH round 1): pooled SWC effect evidence is otherwise unregisterable (ingest gate requires a FAM id). Roll-up rows pool it with family rows; family-scope rows list it as its own scope.

name: Sand dams
definition: Reinforced walls across seasonal sandy riverbeds that trap sand and store water in the sediment aquifer behind them.
dominant_limiting_factor: Drainage-line geomorphology (seasonal sandy channel, bedrock sill) + runoff.
grouping_rationale: Ex-situ channel structure sited on seasonal sand rivers; siting density, not pixel area (added 2026-10-06 from WH round 1: Ritchie 2021, Neufeld 2017; Pete ratified).

name: Subsurface dams
definition: Buried impermeable barriers across alluvial riverbeds that hold water in the alluvium upstream (barragens subterrâneas).
dominant_limiting_factor: Alluvial channel geomorphology + runoff; storage in the alluvium.
grouping_rationale: Ex-situ channel structure sited on alluvial valley bottoms; siting density, not pixel area (added 2026-10-06 from WH round 1: Cirilo 2003, Brito 2007; Pete ratified).

name: Small communal tanks / reservoirs
definition: Village-scale embanked tanks or small reservoirs storing runoff from a larger catchment for multiple uses.
dominant_limiting_factor: Runoff generation + drainage geomorphology + soil clay for storage.
grouping_rationale: Ex-situ storage sited within candidate drainage zones; shares the farm-pond limiter at larger scale (added 2026-10-06 from WH round 1: Saruchera 2019, Verma & Shah 2019; Pete ratified).

name: Cross-cutting envelope (family-agnostic)
definition: Tagging value for evidence applying across ALL forest-restoration families (pooled 'restoration' results that do not isolate planting vs regeneration vs protection), not one subpractice. Not a real subpractice.
dominant_limiting_factor: (cross-cutting — applies to all families)
grouping_rationale: Meta-tag mirroring agroforestry / water-harvesting cross_cutting_envelope (2026-10-06, FR effect round 1): pooled restoration effect evidence is otherwise unregisterable (ingest gate requires a FAM id). Exempt from the qualitative_only parking rule (synthesise-t3t6.py).

name: Plantation forestry (tree farming)
definition: Establishment or management of production tree plantations — commercial/cyclical-harvest planting, monocultures or plantation genera (pine, eucalypt, hybrid poplar, teak, Cedrela) — including afforestation of grasslands/shrublands with plantation species.
dominant_limiting_factor: planting envelope for the production species + management/market feasibility (rotation economics), distinct from restoration-toward-baseline
grouping_rationale: Pete 2026-10-19 (conflict-split ruling 4): plantations are 'tree farming and not forest restoration... How would a plantation restore anything? it is not representative of a natural baseline we are trying to return to. Plantations could potentially provide some meta-population connectivity in the landscape, but still pretty shitty habitat (unless using indigenous and diverse plantings to have a multi-use more bio friendly plantation).' Split from active_planting so plantation evidence cannot set restoration classes; NbS-alignment and roll-up inclusion are the open plantation_rollup decision (Pete + MFL).
